COP rose 0.84% to $136.12 today, recovering modestly from a sharp four-day drop that saw the stock fall 5.6% from $142.28 on November 13th to $134.40 on November 18th. The recovery follows stabilization in oil prices—US crude is now trading at $89.53 per barrel, while global oil stands at $92.94—suggesting the panic selling that drove the earlier decline has eased somewhat, though the stock remains well below where it started the two-week period.

The broader energy sector faces crosscurrents: geopolitical risk in the Middle East (the Strait of Hormuz facing reliability concerns after the Iran war) supports crude prices going forward, while simultaneously, long-term demand pressures are building from energy-intensive AI and data-center expansion that could reshape power grids over the next four years. Near-term European gas stress from low storage and cold weather also supports energy prices, but these moves appear to be reflected incrementally rather than driving sharp daily swings for large-cap oil producers.
